cards.front: What causes a lacunar infarct, and where does it occur?
cards.back: Chronic **hypertension** (and diabetes) damages small penetrating arteries, such as the **lenticulostriate** arteries, by **lipohyalinosis**. Their occlusion leaves small deep cavities in the **basal ganglia**, **internal capsule**, **thalamus** or **pons**.
cards.back_pt: A **hipertensão** crônica (e o diabetes) lesa pequenas artérias perfurantes, como as **lenticuloestriadas**, por **lipo-hialinose**. A oclusão delas deixa pequenas cavidades profundas nos **núcleos da base**, na **cápsula interna**, no **tálamo** ou na **ponte**.

cards.front: In what order do the microscopic changes of a cerebral infarct appear?
cards.back: **12-24 h**: **red neurons** (shrunken, eosinophilic). Then **neutrophils**, then **macrophages** (microglia) that clear the debris; the lipid-rich tissue undergoes **liquefactive necrosis**. Last, **astrocytes** form a **glial scar** around a fluid-filled cavity.
cards.back_pt: **12-24 h**: **neurônios vermelhos** (retraídos, eosinofílicos). Depois **neutrófilos**, e então **macrófagos** (micróglia) que removem os restos; o tecido rico em lipídios sofre **necrose liquefativa**. Por fim, os **astrócitos** formam uma **cicatriz glial** em torno de uma cavidade com líquido.

cards.front: Which deficits suggest a middle cerebral artery (MCA) stroke?
cards.back: Contralateral weakness and sensory loss of the **face and arm** more than the leg. **Dominant** hemisphere (usually left): **aphasia**, Broca (frontal, nonfluent) or Wernicke (temporal, poor comprehension). **Nondominant** hemisphere: **hemineglect**.
cards.back_pt: Fraqueza e perda sensitiva contralaterais de **face e membro superior**, mais do que do membro inferior. Hemisfério **dominante** (geralmente o esquerdo): **afasia**, de Broca (frontal, não fluente) ou de Wernicke (temporal, compreensão ruim). Hemisfério **não dominante**: **heminegligência**.

cards.front: Which deficits suggest an anterior cerebral artery (ACA) stroke?
cards.back: Contralateral weakness and sensory loss of the **leg and foot** (medial motor and sensory cortex). Frontal lobe damage can also cause **abulia** (lack of will and initiative) and urinary incontinence.
cards.back_pt: Fraqueza e perda sensitiva contralaterais de **membro inferior e pé** (córtex motor e sensitivo medial). A lesão do lobo frontal também pode causar **abulia** (falta de vontade e iniciativa) e incontinência urinária.

cards.front: Which deficits suggest a posterior cerebral artery (PCA) stroke?
cards.back: Contralateral **homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing** (occipital cortex; the macular area often keeps collateral flow from the MCA). A dominant-side PCA stroke that also involves the **splenium** of the corpus callosum causes **alexia without agraphia**.
cards.back_pt: **Hemianopsia homônima** contralateral **com preservação macular** (córtex occipital; a área macular costuma manter fluxo colateral da ACM). Um AVC da ACP do lado dominante que também atinge o **esplênio** do corpo caloso causa **alexia sem agrafia**.

cards.front: What are the source, risk groups and CT shape of a subdural hematoma?
cards.back: Torn **bridging veins** between the cortex and the dural sinuses. Risk: **elderly** people and **alcoholics** (brain atrophy stretches the veins), and **shaken babies**. CT: a **crescent-shaped** collection that **crosses suture lines**.
cards.back_pt: Ruptura das **veias-ponte** entre o córtex e os seios durais. Risco: **idosos** e **etilistas** (a atrofia cerebral estira as veias), e **bebês sacudidos** (*shaken baby*). TC: coleção **em crescente** que **cruza as linhas de sutura**.

cards.front: Why can a patient develop a new focal deficit several days after a subarachnoid hemorrhage?
cards.back: **Vasospasm**: blood breakdown products around the cerebral arteries make them constrict, which causes **delayed cerebral ischemia**. Other causes of worsening are **rebleeding**, **hydrocephalus** and **hyponatremia**.
cards.back_pt: **Vasoespasmo**: os produtos de degradação do sangue ao redor das artérias cerebrais causam sua constrição, o que leva a **isquemia cerebral tardia**. Outras causas de piora são **ressangramento**, **hidrocefalia** e **hiponatremia**.

cards.front: How do hypertensive and amyloid intraparenchymal hemorrhages differ?
cards.back: **Hypertensive**: rupture of **Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms** of small penetrating arteries; deep sites: **basal ganglia** (putamen), **thalamus**, pons, cerebellum. **Cerebral amyloid angiopathy**: β-amyloid in cortical vessel walls of older adults; **lobar** hemorrhages that often recur.
cards.back_pt: **Hipertensiva**: ruptura de **microaneurismas de Charcot-Bouchard** de pequenas artérias perfurantes; locais profundos: **núcleos da base** (putâmen), **tálamo**, ponte, cerebelo. **Angiopatia amiloide cerebral**: β-amiloide na parede de vasos corticais de idosos; hemorragias **lobares** que costumam recorrer.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with hypertension has sudden vertigo, nausea and trouble swallowing. His voice is hoarse. Exam shows nystagmus, a small left pupil with mild left ptosis, and loss of pain and temperature sensation on the left side of the face and the right side of the body. He has ataxia of the left arm and leg and a reduced left gag reflex. Facial movements are symmetric, strength is normal in all limbs, and hearing is normal. Occlusion of which artery best explains these findings?
questions.explanation: This is the **lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome** from **PICA** occlusion. Damage to the **nucleus ambiguus** causes dysphagia, hoarseness and a weak gag; the spinal trigeminal nucleus and spinothalamic tract give crossed pain and temperature loss; descending sympathetic fibers give **Horner syndrome**. An AICA (lateral pontine) stroke also causes vertigo and crossed sensory loss, but it adds ipsilateral **facial paralysis** and **hearing loss**, not dysphagia and hoarseness.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **síndrome bulbar lateral (de Wallenberg)** por oclusão da **PICA** (artéria cerebelar posteroinferior). A lesão do **núcleo ambíguo** causa disfagia, rouquidão e reflexo nauseoso fraco; o núcleo espinal do trigêmeo e o trato espinotalâmico explicam a perda cruzada de dor e temperatura; as fibras simpáticas descendentes explicam a **síndrome de Horner**. Um AVC da AICA (artéria cerebelar anteroinferior; pontino lateral) também causa vertigem e perda sensitiva cruzada, mas acrescenta **paralisia facial** e **perda auditiva** ipsilaterais, e não disfagia e rouquidão.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man is hit on the right side of the head by a baseball. He loses consciousness for about 1 minute, then wakes up and talks normally for 2 hours. He then develops a severe headache and vomiting and becomes drowsy. His right pupil is dilated and reacts poorly to light. CT of the head shows a fracture of the right temporal bone and a hyperdense, biconvex (lens-shaped) collection under it that does not cross the suture lines. Which vessel is the most likely source of the bleeding?
choices: Bridging veins between the cortex and the dural sinuses
questions.explanation: Trauma to the **pterion** with a temporal bone fracture, a **lucid interval** and a **biconvex** collection limited by the sutures is an **epidural hematoma** from the **middle meningeal artery**. Arterial pressure separates the dura from the skull, and the dura is firmly attached at the sutures, so the blood cannot cross them. Torn **bridging veins** cause a subdural hematoma, which is **crescent-shaped** and crosses sutures. The dilated pupil suggests early uncal herniation compressing the oculomotor nerve.
questions.explanation_pt: Trauma no **ptério** com fratura do osso temporal, **intervalo lúcido** e coleção **biconvexa** limitada pelas suturas é um **hematoma epidural (extradural)** pela **artéria meníngea média**. A pressão arterial descola a dura-máter do crânio, e a dura está firmemente presa nas suturas, por isso o sangue não as cruza. A ruptura das **veias-ponte** causa hematoma subdural, que tem forma **em crescente** e cruza as suturas. A pupila dilatada sugere herniação uncal inicial comprimindo o nervo oculomotor.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man has a sudden, severe headache while lifting weights. He calls it the worst headache of his life. He vomits and has neck stiffness. He has had high blood pressure since adolescence. Blood pressure in the right arm is 172/96 mm Hg. Femoral pulses are weak and delayed. An old chest x-ray showed notching of the lower rib borders. CT of the head shows hyperdense blood in the basal cisterns and Sylvian fissures, with no focal hematoma in the brain tissue. Rupture of which lesion most likely caused this bleeding?
choices: Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysm of a lenticulostriate artery
Bridging vein between the cortex and a dural sinus
Branch of the middle meningeal artery
Saccular aneurysm at the anterior communicating artery junction
questions.explanation: Sudden 'worst headache of life' with blood in the basal cisterns is a **subarachnoid hemorrhage**, most often from a ruptured **saccular (berry) aneurysm** at a branch point of the circle of Willis, most commonly the **anterior communicating artery**. His weak femoral pulses and rib notching point to **coarctation of the aorta**, a known association of berry aneurysms. Hypertension also causes **Charcot-Bouchard** microaneurysms, but these bleed into the deep brain tissue (basal ganglia, thalamus), not into the subarachnoid cisterns.
questions.explanation_pt: Cefaleia súbita, 'a pior da vida', com sangue nas cisternas da base é uma **hemorragia subaracnóidea**, geralmente por ruptura de **aneurisma sacular** (*berry aneurysm*) em um ponto de ramificação do polígono de Willis, mais comumente na **artéria comunicante anterior**. Os pulsos femorais fracos e as erosões costais indicam **coarctação da aorta**, associação conhecida dos aneurismas saculares. A hipertensão também causa microaneurismas de **Charcot-Bouchard**, mas estes sangram no parênquima profundo (núcleos da base, tálamo), e não nas cisternas subaracnóideas.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old right-handed woman with atrial fibrillation is brought in 1 hour after the sudden onset of left-sided weakness. Exam shows weakness and sensory loss of the left face and left arm; the left leg is only mildly weak. She does not look toward people standing on her left, and when asked to mark the middle of a horizontal line she marks it far to the right. She denies that anything is wrong. Her speech is fluent, and she follows commands and repeats sentences normally. Occlusion of which artery best explains these findings?
questions.explanation: Contralateral **face and arm** weakness and sensory loss point to the **MCA** territory. **Hemineglect** and denial of the deficit with normal language point to the **nondominant (right) parietal lobe** in a right-handed person; an embolus from atrial fibrillation is a typical cause. A left MCA stroke would cause **right-sided** weakness and **aphasia**. A right ACA stroke would weaken the left **leg** more than the arm.
questions.explanation_pt: Fraqueza e perda sensitiva contralaterais de **face e membro superior** indicam o território da **ACM**. **Heminegligência** e negação do déficit com linguagem normal indicam o **lobo parietal não dominante (direito)** em uma pessoa destra; um êmbolo da fibrilação atrial é uma causa típica. Um AVC da ACM esquerda causaria fraqueza **à direita** e **afasia**. Um AVC da ACA direita afetaria mais o **membro inferior** esquerdo do que o superior.

notes.title: Cerebrovascular disease: stroke syndromes and intracranial hemorrhage
notes.body_md:
## Ischemic stroke

- **Thrombotic**: atherosclerosis of the carotid or large intracranial arteries. Often preceded by a **TIA** (brief focal deficit without infarction on imaging).
- **Embolic**: from the heart (atrial fibrillation; see the arrhythmias block) or a carotid plaque.
- **Lacunar**: hypertensive **lipohyalinosis** of penetrating arteries; internal capsule infarct gives **pure motor hemiparesis**.
- **Vascular dementia**: many infarcts over time, with **stepwise** decline.
- The infarct undergoes **liquefactive necrosis** and ends as a cavity (pseudocyst) lined by a **glial scar**.

## Syndromes by artery

- **MCA**: contralateral face and arm deficits; aphasia (dominant) or hemineglect (nondominant).
- **ACA**: contralateral leg deficits, abulia.
- **PCA**: homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.
- **Basilar** (ventral pons): **locked-in syndrome**; quadriplegia, but consciousness, blinking and vertical eye movements are preserved.
- **PICA** (lateral medulla, **Wallenberg**): dysphagia, hoarseness, crossed pain and temperature loss, **Horner**, vertigo, nystagmus.
- **AICA** (lateral pons): vertigo, ataxia, crossed pain and temperature loss and Horner, but ipsilateral **facial paralysis** and **hearing loss** instead of dysphagia and hoarseness.
- **Anterior spinal artery** (medial medulla): contralateral hemiparesis and loss of position and vibration sense, tongue deviates to the lesion side.

## Intracranial hemorrhage

- **Epidural**: **middle meningeal artery**, fracture at the **pterion**, **lucid interval**, **biconvex** shape that stops at sutures.
- **Subdural**: **bridging veins**, **crescent** shape that crosses sutures.
- **Subarachnoid**: ruptured **berry aneurysm**, most often at the **anterior communicating artery**; 'worst headache of life', **xanthochromia** in the CSF, later **vasospasm**. Associations: **ADPKD** (see the renal block), **Ehlers-Danlos**, **coarctation**.
- **Intraparenchymal**: hypertension (**Charcot-Bouchard** microaneurysms; basal ganglia, thalamus) or **amyloid angiopathy** (lobar).

## Other

- **Venous sinus thrombosis**: hypercoagulable states (pregnancy, oral contraceptives); headache, papilledema, seizures, hemorrhagic infarcts.
- **Cerebral edema**: **cytotoxic** (cell swelling, early ischemia) or **vasogenic** (leaky blood-brain barrier; tumors, abscess).
- Herniation syndromes: see the CNS tumors and trauma block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## AVC isquêmico

- **Trombótico**: aterosclerose da carótida ou de grandes artérias intracranianas. Muitas vezes precedido por **AIT** (déficit focal breve sem infarto na imagem).
- **Embólico**: de origem cardíaca (fibrilação atrial; ver o bloco de arritmias) ou de placa carotídea.
- **Lacunar**: **lipo-hialinose** hipertensiva de artérias perfurantes; o infarto da cápsula interna causa **hemiparesia motora pura**.
- **Demência vascular**: vários infartos ao longo do tempo, com declínio **em degraus**.
- O infarto sofre **necrose liquefativa** e termina como uma cavidade (pseudocisto) revestida por **cicatriz glial**.

## Síndromes por artéria

- **ACM**: déficits contralaterais de face e membro superior; afasia (dominante) ou heminegligência (não dominante).
- **ACA**: déficits contralaterais do membro inferior, abulia.
- **ACP**: hemianopsia homônima com preservação macular.
- **Basilar** (ponte ventral): **síndrome do encarceramento** (*locked-in*); tetraplegia, mas com consciência, piscar e movimentos oculares verticais preservados.
- **PICA** (bulbo lateral, **Wallenberg**): disfagia, rouquidão, perda cruzada de dor e temperatura, **Horner**, vertigem, nistagmo.
- **AICA** (ponte lateral): vertigem, ataxia, perda cruzada de dor e temperatura e Horner, mas com **paralisia facial** e **perda auditiva** ipsilaterais em vez de disfagia e rouquidão.
- **Artéria espinal anterior** (bulbo medial): hemiparesia contralateral e perda da propriocepção e da sensibilidade vibratória; a língua desvia para o lado da lesão.

## Hemorragia intracraniana

- **Epidural (extradural)**: **artéria meníngea média**, fratura no **ptério**, **intervalo lúcido**, forma **biconvexa** que para nas suturas.
- **Subdural**: **veias-ponte**, forma **em crescente** que cruza as suturas.
- **Subaracnóidea**: ruptura de **aneurisma sacular** (*berry*), mais frequente na **artéria comunicante anterior**; 'a pior cefaleia da vida', **xantocromia** no LCR, depois **vasoespasmo**. Associações: **DRPAD** (ver o bloco renal), **Ehlers-Danlos**, **coarctação da aorta**.
- **Intraparenquimatosa**: hipertensão (microaneurismas de **Charcot-Bouchard**; núcleos da base, tálamo) ou **angiopatia amiloide** (lobar).

## Outros

- **Trombose venosa cerebral**: estados de hipercoagulabilidade (gestação, contraceptivos orais); cefaleia, papiledema, crises epilépticas, infartos hemorrágicos.
- **Edema cerebral**: **citotóxico** (edema celular, isquemia inicial) ou **vasogênico** (barreira hematoencefálica permeável; tumores, abscesso).
- Síndromes de herniação: ver o bloco de tumores e trauma do SNC.
